 Follow GTA 6 hacker behind original 2022 leaks pleads guilty just days ahead of game’s launch
 Scott Duwe Mon, November 16, 2026 at 3:04 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Image via Rockstar Games The hacker behind a massive Grand Theft Auto 6 leak that revealed in-development footage of the game before its official reveal back in 2022 has plead guilty to their crimes.
 Arion Kurtaj, now 21 years old, was initially sentenced to a hospital stay due to his severe autism and also being underage, but was since deemed fit to stand trial earlier this year and released to a normal prison. Today, he plead guilty, and sentencing will come at a later date, according to a report by BBC .
 Image via Rockstar Games
 "He sat in the dock with short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt but no tie," BBC's report described. "The now 21-year-old blinked frequently during the hearing and stood to confirm his name, and pled guilty to all counts with no visible emotion."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In 2022, Kurtaj (then 16), was under police custody for other hacking offenses he committed during his time with hacker group Lapsus$, but was able to breach Rockstar Games while using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel TV.
 He subsequently leaked 90 clips of GTA 6's early builds after hacking into Rockstar Games' slack and posting a ransom message, to which the company did not comply. BBC said Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to "physical assaults on workers whilst in custody including multiple biting incidents."
 The leaked videos four years ago showed protagonists Jason and Lucia moving around Vice City in the dev build, revealing a lot about the game before Rockstar had its own chance to showcase what it had been working on for several years already at that time.
 GTA 6 launches this week on Nov. 19 after officially being revealed in December 2023, just over a year after Kurtaj's leaks hit the internet, and is expected to generate billions in revenue.
